newsitem.title: UK: London platinum sinks to fresh near 3-year low.
newsitem.headline: London platinum sinks to fresh near 3-year low.

text.p: Platinum fixed at $376.35 an ounce Wednesday afternoon, the lowest since December 7, 1993, after losing more ground on the back of weakness in the gold market.
Platinum prices had declined $1.40 since fixing at $377.75 an ounce in the morning, which had been the lowest level since December 8, 1995.
London platinum sinks to fresh near 3-year low
Dealers said there was no recent news or fundamental reason for platinum prices to sink to fresh three-year lows outside of overwhelmingly bearish market sentiment across the precious metals complex.
"There's nothing fundamental pushing platinum and palladium lower. They're just being sucked down by the bearish sentiment surrounding gold," a London based dealer said.
Technical analysts pegged platinum's near term support at $375 an ounce ahead of an eventual target of $370 an ounce. It had been bid as low as $375.75 an ounce before the fixing.
Its sister metal palladium fixed at $114.50 an ounce, compared to $114.75 in the morning, the lowest fixings since April 20, 1995.
